Commentary.Commentary: We witnessed some scintillating cricket today and it was a high voltage match. Do join us for the 2nd ODI at 1400 IST scheduled to be played at the same venue on 9th October. Till then, goodbye and take care!

MAN OF THE MATCH, JAKE BALL says that he was just thinking of running in and hitting the deck hard at that stage (at the death). On the overall bowling in this innings, he feels that change of pace was the key. On the transition from county cricket to international cricket, he admits that it is a huge difference and the conditions were really tough. He says that they never gave up hope even at 271/4 and felt that if they could take a couple of wickets, they could spring a collapse.

England captain, JOS BUTTLER feels that it's been a fantastic game. Stokes pulled everyone together and batted brilliantly. Adds that Jake Ball was superb on his debut. Adds that he was put under pressure by the home side but he responded really well and deserved the fifer. (On Ben Duckett) Says that he didn't look like he was on his debut. He was looking like a seasoned pro out there. (On him dropping Kayes) Says that it was a very easy catch and he didn't know how he dropped that!

Bangladesh captain, MASHRAFE MORTAZA says that it could have been an easy game to win but they made it difficult for themselves by losing wickets in clusters. Feels that it was a nice wicket to bat upon and praises Kayes and Shakib for their batting. Laments the dropped catches and admits a target under 300 could have been achievable. Feels happy for Kayes for his back-to-back hundreds (He hit one in the warm-up game). Does not feel there was enough dew to trouble the bowlers.

Earlier, England batted brilliantly to score 309 riding on Stokes' ton with half centuries from Duckett and Buttler. It was always going to be a tricky chase for the home side. Kayes batted brilliantly to begin with but he lost his touch as he started cramping up. He scored a century but it was not enough as the home side eventually crumbled under pressure and handed England a victory. Even Shakib suffered cramps and that had a toll on the match.

What a match and England have pulled off a victory from the jaws of defeat! At one moment, when Kayes and Shakib were out in the middle they looked comfortable and were on track but as Shakib fell to Jake Ball, the match turned on its head and the home side fell like a pack of cards. Ball and Rashid bowled brilliantly and scalped five and four wickets respectively. Jake Ball was the star of the show as he became the first English bowler to take a fifer on his ODI debut.

OUT! ENGLAND WIN BY 21 RUNS!! Third time lucky for Ball and he becomes the FIRST ENGLISH PLAYER TO TAKE A 5-FER ON ODI DEBUT! FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Shakib crashes it through the covers, past a diving Ben Stokes. Substitute Sam Billings dives at the fence but in vain! 14 from that over, 39 off the last 3!

FOUR! Short and outside off, Shakib cuts it behind point for a boundary!

Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
On middle, clipped through mid-wicket for a run.

Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.

Full and down the leg side, Tamim misses his flick and the ball goes off his thigh pads back to the bowler.
On a good length on middle and leg, defended watchfully.

UPPISH... LANDS SAFE AGAIN! Kayes is toying with his luck here. A short ball around off, he goes for the pull but does not hit it well enough and luckily for him, the ball lands well short of Moeen Ali at the mid-wicket fence. A single taken.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Jake Ball comes into the attack.

IN THE AIR... SAFE! What an over from Woakes. Could have had both the openers but for some luck. A good short ball around middle, Kayes goes for the pull but mistimes it. There is a man in the deep at mid-wicket but the ball does not carry to him. A run taken.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly but straight to mid off for a quick run.

EDGED, BUT SAFE! On a good length on middle, Iqbal looks to steer it to third man again but is cramped for room and gets a healthy outside edge. But it does not carry to Buttler! Woakes is frustrated. He is working up Tamim here.

Swing and a miss. Sends a telepathic message a month early that he is going to come down the track. Woakes bangs it short and Tamim has no where to go. Looks to hop and steer it to third man but misses. Woakes has a word with Tamim, egging him on to go for the attack.
Landed outside off, slashed hard down to Adil Rashid at third man. A single is the result.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Down the leg side, Tamim feasts on it and tickles it past short fine leg for a boundary! 14 from the over, 268 more needed from 252 balls now!

On a good length this time, angling into the batsman, IK looks to work it to the leg side but misses. The ball goes off his thighs to point and the batsmen take a single. Tamim charged for the single but Kayes was not too keen. He stuttered but then eventually went for the single. The fielder returned a weak under-arm throw at the bowler's end and that gave enough time for Kayes to get in.

LEADING EDGE... NEARLY CARRIES! On a good length around middle, Imrul looks to work it to the leg side but is a tad early into it. The ball goes off the leading edge but does not carry to James Vince at short extra cover.
Slip goes to short extra cover now.
SIX! Thump! Full and around off, Kayes gets down and mows it over deep mid-wicket, clearing Moeen Ali with ease! They needed that. Kayes moves to 22 but it has taken 21 balls.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single. 279 more needed from 256 balls now.
Full and wide outside off, Tamim slashes hard and mistimes it over point. Gets a couple.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Comes down the track and has a swing but misses.
Outside off, steered to third man for one.
A length ball outside off, IK backs away and slashes hard but gets a bottom edge which goes on the bounce to the keeper.
WIDE. A short ball around leg, Imrul goes for the hook but misses.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and wide outside off, Imrul has a slash but gets a thick outside edge to third man. A run taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! It is a hack but Kayes and Bangladesh could care less at the moment. A length ball on middle, Kayes heaves hard and the ball goes off the inner half of the bat through mid-wicket. There are only three men on the leg side - a deep square leg, a short fine leg and a mid on. The ball finds the ropes. 286 more needed from 266 balls now.
Full and wide outside off, a slash and a miss.
Outside off, run down to third man for a single.
Full and wide outside off, a slash and a miss.
Landed around off, played straight to point. A MAIDEN OVER!
On a good length around middle, angling away, blocked towards point.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman comes down the track but misses it completely.
Fuller this time, pushed towards cover.
On a good length around middle and leg, defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! Wrong line again and this time Tamim makes him pay. Down the leg side, tucked past short fine leg for a boundary.

Kayes misses out on this one. Banged in short and going down the leg side, Kayes goes for the pull but is perhaps a tad early into the stroke. The ball goes off his gloves but does not carry to short fine leg. The batsmen take a single but a leg bye has been signalled.
Full and straight, defended towards short mid-wicket.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly but straight to mid off.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and on middle and off, driven back to the bowler.
Digs it in short, Tamim goes for the pull but misses it completely.
Outside off, another play and a miss.
On a good length on middle, Iqbal looks to work it to the leg side but misses and gets a leading edge to cover.
Full and outside off, Tamim feels for it but is beaten.
Down the leg side, Tamim looks to flick but misses and the ball goes off his pads towards square leg. A leg bye taken. So it is a maiden for Willey but not for England.
Outside off again, not played at once more. 5 dot balls in the over.
Action replay of the previous ball.
Outside off, left alone.
Half volley outside off, driven beautifully but straight to short cover.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
David Willey to bowl from the other end.

EDGED! FOUR! In high school they call it an educated edge. It means the batsman was anyways trying to play it in that region but still got an edge. Well, as far as the bowler is concerned, it was an edge which did not go to hand. Kayes looked to open the face of the bat and run it down to third man but was beaten by pace. The ball went off the outside edge, wide of second slip and then to the third man fence. 299 more needed from 294 balls now.
On a good length around off, angling away, IK has a feel for it but misses.
Full and wide outside off, Imrul has a slash but misses.
Where is the ball? Everyone is searching for it. Ahhh... here it is. It was stuck in the stands! Umpire Erasmus has a smile on his face.

SIX! Thrash! Goodness me! Kayes has surprised not one but plenty of people. Everyone perhaps expected Tamim to start off aggressively but we have a change in ploy here. Around middle and leg, a length between full and good, Kayes just flicks it but the timing is immense and the ball sails over mid-wicket!
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
On middle, tucked through square leg for a single.
TAMIM IQBAL and IMRUL KAYES are the openers for the home side. CHRIS WOAKES to start off proceedings to Tamim with two slips in place. Here we go...

The players are back out in the middle. Can 310 be chased down? Or will England take a 1-0 series lead? Bangladesh will have to bat well but with dew imminent, the English bowlers will have to bowl nicely too.
